html:
SMTO-MEM-0022 — Indexing stopped before it finished

GUID: 52ac66ed-e6d0-5e65-8d95-420d3635ef50
Slug: knowledge-indexing-cancelled
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • SMTO stopped making this source searchable before it finished. This happens when indexing is cancelled, the file is replaced or deleted, its conversation is deleted, settings change, or SMTO shuts down.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Knowledge, find the document. If you replaced, deleted or cancelled it on purpose, you don't need to do anything. A newer upload or reindex has already taken over from the stopped attempt.
  2. Otherwise, on the document select Manage, then Reindex. SMTO doesn't restart a stopped attempt by itself; Reindex starts a new one.
  3. For memories, open Knowledge › Semantic memory and select Retry Memory indexing if it is shown. Memory indexing stops when its settings change and needs a new attempt.

What success looks like

  • The document shows Ready to search, or the Memory status shows Memory index is up to date.

If it still fails

  • If indexing keeps stopping without anyone cancelling it, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; SMTO may be shutting down or restarting. Don't delete the source to clear this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The indexing job raised indexing_cancelled because it was cancelled, the Server is stopping, the document was deleted or superseded by a newer job, its conversation was deleted, or (for Memory) the generation or Memory settings changed.

What this means

  • This attempt stopped before finishing its search data. Starting a new indexing attempt is an explicit action. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported indexing_cancelled. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The new indexing attempt reaches Ready.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Check the job state and the document's current job_id in /api/agent/rag/jobs. Superseded attempts need no action; if the stop was unintended, start a new attempt with the document's Reindex action or Retry Memory indexing.
  • Open the affected source in Knowledge and choose Manage → Reindex when you want to resume.

Retry and execution caution

  • The new indexing attempt reaches Ready.

How to verify the fix

  • The new indexing attempt reaches Ready.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
